newsitem.title: USA: Slaying of real estate mogul a mystery.
newsitem.headline: Slaying of real estate mogul a mystery.

text.p: Police said Monday they had no suspects in the killing of a real estate tycoon who once had plans to build what would have been the world's tallest office tower.
The body of Lee Miglin, 72, was found in the garage of his home Sunday in a prestigious neighbourhood north of downtown Chicago. His throat was slashed and his car was missing.
Police said Monday they had not found the car and had no one in particular under suspicion. His wife, who was out of town, called police on returning when she could not locate her husband.
She told the Chicago Sun-Times it appeared the killer or killers may have spent the night in the house after the crime, which apparently occurred Saturday night.

Miglin was chairman of Miglin-Beitler Inc., a real estate development company. A decade ago the company announced plans to build a 125-floor office tower in downtown Chicago that at the time would have been the world's tallest such structure.
Plans for the building were later abandoned.
